name: Commodity time-series momentum

origin.source_title: Time Series Momentum (Journal of Financial Economics)

how_it_works.simple: Look at each commodity, like oil or wheat. If its price rose over the last year, buy it; if it fell, sell it.
how_it_works.analogy: Like a weather forecaster who says tomorrow will be like the last few days, and is right more often than not.
how_it_works.precise: For each commodity future, the sign of its trailing 12-month excess return sets a long or short position, scaled to a constant ex ante volatility, with a one month holding period. Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen find that commodity TSMOM has a significant alpha (0.57% per month) even after controlling for cross-sectional commodity momentum.

rule: Each month, for each commodity future, go long if its past 12-month excess return is positive and short if negative; size each position at 40% annualized ex ante volatility divided by the number of contracts (or scale the sleeve to a target); hold one month.
data_needed: Rolled front-month commodity futures returns, daily
economic_rationale: Slow diffusion of supply and demand news and hedger flows make commodity trends persist; speculators profit from TSMOM at the expense of hedgers (Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen 2012).
why_it_might_fail: Commodity trends reverse sharply around supply shocks and policy events; in AQR's own data the commodity sleeve earned a Sharpe ratio of about 0.21 from 2012 to mid 2026, versus about 1.0 before 2010 (catalog computation).

reported_results.source: Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen (2012), TSMOM vs XSMOM regression table, Panel A
reported_results.notes: Regression of commodity TSMOM on cross-sectional commodity momentum: monthly intercept (alpha) 0.57%, t = 4.43. No Sharpe ratio for the commodity sleeve was read on the page.

post_publication_evidence: The commodity sleeve of AQR's TSMOM data dropped from a Sharpe ratio near 1.0 (1985 to 2009) to about 0.21 (2012 to 2026-05) in the catalog's computation. McLean and Pontiff (2016) find that across 97 published stock return predictors, portfolio returns are 26% lower out of sample and 58% lower after publication (https://doi.org/10.1111/jofi.12365).

implementations.notes: Futures trading framework by Rob Carver; the provided rules folder includes ewmac.py (trend) and carry.py. Repo moved from robcarver17/pysystemtrade.

relevance.reason: Commodity trends feed commodity currencies (AUD, CAD, NOK), so this is a useful signal source and comparison for parity.
